summary.whatChanges: Adds a public `withParser(schema, parser)` API (plus the `INVALID` sentinel) that installs an externally generated synchronous parser as a schema's fast path, returning a clone. `compile()` is refactored to build on it, then overrides the validator with its generated assert-only variant. Both helpers are re-exported from zod classic and zod/mini.
behaviorChanges: `z.withParser(schema, parser)` is available: returns a clone whose parse/safeParse, Standard Schema validate, and z.parse use the supplied parser, leaving the original schema untouched
`INVALID` is exported publicly; a supplied parser returning it defers to the normal Zod runtime so callers still get real ZodError issues
`withParser` throws `ZodCompileUnsupportedError` for schemas containing a reference cycle (recursive/lazy)
Supplied parsers are bypassed for async parses, backward direction/encode, skipChecks, and fallback re-entry, which run on the runtime instead
`z.validate()` on a withParser clone answers via the supplied parser
risks: A supplied parser that succeeds with a value contradicting the schema is returned to callers unchecked at runtime (only the TS signature guards it), so parse() can return a wrongly typed value
Docs note the parser must build fresh output rather than return its input; violating this is undetectable and can leak/alias caller objects
compile() now routes through withParser's recursive-schema check, so recursion failures surface from a different code path (swallowed unless options.strict)
Truncated diff hides whether installCompiledUserMethods and validator wiring behave identically for compile() after the refactor
